title: Inoculation and co-inoculation of two monosporic fungi onto surface-sterile blackberry fruits for quantification experiments
author: Hilje-Rodríguez, Molina-Bravo
materials: For fungal cultures, potato dextrose agar (PDA) media (Oxoid Ltd., ThermoScientific™) was prepared by adding 39g of the selected media to 1L of ultrapure water. Complete medium dissolution was achieved by slowly mixing and heating the mixture. The prepared medium was sterilized by autoclaving at 121 °C for 20 min. Sterile PDA media was allowed to cool to around 50 °C and poured into sterile Petri dishes (200 × 15mm) (20 mL per plate) previously dripped with 25% lactic acid inside a laminar flow cabinet. Water agar (WA) (Oxoid Ltd., ThermoScientific™) media was prepared by adding 30g of agar to 1L of ultrapure water and autoclaved. For monosporic cultures and inoculation assays, prepared WA medium was poured into sterile Petri dishes (200 × 15mm and 60 × 15mm; 20 and 10 mL per plate respectively) previously dripped with 25% lactic acid. To immobilize berries, holes were punched in the center of the 60 × 15mm Petri dishes using a 10 mm width stainless steel cork borer.

steps.title: Prepare PDA medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve 39 g potato dextrose agar (Oxoid Ltd., ThermoScientific™) in 1 L ultrapure water, mix slowly while heating, autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min, then cool to ~50 °C.

steps.title: Dispense PDA into plates
steps.instruction: In a laminar flow cabinet, drip sterile 200 × 15 mm Petri dishes with 25 % lactic acid, then pour 20 mL of the cooled PDA into each plate.

steps.title: Prepare water agar plates
steps.instruction: Dissolve 30 g agar (Oxoid Ltd., ThermoScientific™) in 1 L ultrapure water, autoclave, then pour into sterile Petri dishes previously dripped with 25 % lactic acid: 20 mL per 200 × 15 mm plate and 10 mL per 60 × 15 mm plate.

steps.title: Punch holes for berries
steps.instruction: Using a 10 mm stainless‑steel cork borer, punch a central hole in each 60 × 15 mm water‑agar plate to immobilize berries.

steps.title: Isolate Botrytis cinerea from berries
steps.instruction: With a sterile dissecting needle, transfer mycelia and conidia from infected blackberry fruits onto a microscope slide, confirm identity, then place onto sterile 200 × 15 mm Petri dishes containing 20 mL PDA + 25 % lactic acid.

steps.title: Incubate initial B. cinerea culture
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates at 25 °C in the dark for at least 3 days.

steps.title: Purify B. cinerea by subculture
steps.instruction: Transfer a portion of the grown mycelium to fresh sterile 200 × 15 mm plates with 20 mL PDA + 25 % lactic acid and incubate at 25 °C with a 12 h light/12 h dark photoperiod until a uniform lawn forms.

steps.title: Obtain monosporic B. cinerea cultures
steps.instruction: Prepare a conidia suspension (see step 9), spread it on sterile 200 × 15 mm water‑agar plates (20 mL) with a cotton swab, leave overnight, observe germination within 24 h, pick individual germinating spores with a dissecting needle and transfer each onto a fresh PDA + 25 % lactic acid plate; incubate at 25 °C with a 12 h photoperiod.

steps.title: Reactivate Trichoderma atroviride isolate
steps.instruction: Retrieve the isolate stored at 4 °C in vials containing PDA + 25 % lactic acid and mineral oil, decant the oil, place fungal tissue portions onto sterile 200 × 15 mm plates with 20 mL PDA + 25 % lactic acid, and incubate as for B. cinerea. Obtain pure monosporic cultures by the same single‑spore isolation procedure described above.

steps.title: Prepare conidia suspensions
steps.instruction: From each monosporic culture, scrape conidia off the plate surface with a sterile loop into a beaker containing sterile distilled water, shake to disperse aggregates, count spores using a drop in a Neubauer haemocytometer, then dilute with sterile distilled water to a final concentration of 1 × 10⁶ conidia / mL.
